items.stem: A developer wants Copilot to follow the repository's naming and error-handling conventions automatically. What is the most durable approach?

options.text: Add repository custom instructions that state the conventions, and still review output
options.rationale: Correct: custom instructions steer generation repo-wide, but review remains required.

options.text: Paste the conventions into every chat prompt by hand
options.rationale: Manual repetition is error-prone and not durable.

options.text: Rename files until Copilot infers the style
Disable Copilot and write all code manually
options.rationale: That abandons the tool rather than configuring it.

items.explanation: Correct: custom instructions steer generation repo-wide, but review remains required.

items.stem: A coding agent will open pull requests from issues in a protected repository. Which TWO controls keep this safe? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Require human review and passing checks before any agent PR merges
options.rationale: Correct: human review plus required checks gate AI changes.

options.text: Scope each issue narrowly so the agent's change surface is bounded
options.rationale: Correct: a bounded, well-specified issue limits risk.

options.text: Allow the agent to push directly to the default branch
Give the agent admin rights to adjust its own checks

items.explanation: Correct: human review plus required checks gate AI changes.

items.stem: Generations keep ignoring the team's logging convention despite a custom-instructions file. What should you check first?

options.text: Whether the instruction file is in the expected path and scope, and whether the convention is stated unambiguously
options.rationale: Correct: path, scope and clarity determine whether instructions take effect.

options.text: Whether the repository has enough stars
options.rationale: Popularity is irrelevant to instruction handling.

options.text: Whether to raise the model temperature
Whether to delete the file and rely on chat memory

items.explanation: Correct: path, scope and clarity determine whether instructions take effect.
